numbers.name: no_feedback_limit
numbers.value: beta = 0: feedback integrator equals the layer 3 integrator without feedback at 20 random sets (rel < 1e-6)

numbers.name: steady_trace
numbers.value: one type alone: integrated trace equals the upper root of kappa E = w (S - delta R*(E)) at 20 random sets (rel < 1e-6)

numbers.name: critical_supply
numbers.value: S_c = delta R*_1 + kappa (R*_2(0)/R*_1 - 1)/(w beta_2): invasion rate of the trace-helped type is zero at S_c, negative at 0.99 S_c, positive at S_c/0.99 (20 random sets)

numbers.name: hysteresis_window
numbers.value: 4 random sets with S_b < 0.95 S_c (window width 7 to 11 percent of S_c): supply lowered from 1.4 S_c into the window keeps type 2, raised from 0.7 S_b keeps type 1; above S_c type 2 wins from either order

numbers.name: negative_control
numbers.value: beta_2 = 0: both supply paths end with type 1 (no switch, no hysteresis)

numbers.name: obligate_succession
numbers.value: S_c < S < delta R*_2(0): type 2 alone dies out, after a type-1 pioneer it takes over (4 random sets)

note: Derivation and numerical check; no external data. Author (2026-11-19): the trace feeds back by changing the environment of later systems, not as a force. The linear form a_i(E) = a_i0 (1 + beta_i E), trace written in proportion to resource used (w) and fading at kappa is an AI choice of the simplest form. Without feedback the lowest-R* type wins at every supply and from every history; with feedback the winner depends on the supply (switch at S_c), on the supply's history (hysteresis between S_b and S_c) and a later type may need a pioneer. Nearest known theory: niche construction, facilitation in succession (Connell and Slatyer 1977), plant-soil feedback and alternative stable states; those give the same kinds of behaviour. The UET-specific part would be w set by energy use (bits per joule); not tested here. Next: a Test Card on data where the supply was raised and lowered (hysteresis) with known trace effects.
